children: Sen.
Adam Schiff
(D-Calif.) said artificial intelligence companies should help shoulder the economic costs of AI’s rollout while calling for tax reforms to address America’s growing wealth inequality.
Schiff Calls For AI Companies To Share Costs
On Saturday, Schiff made the remarks in a post on
X
while discussing how the U.S. should pay for the broader economic effects of AI.
"AI companies shouldn’t be able to push their costs off onto everyday Americans," he said.
He added that the country needs "a truly progressive tax code" that works for ordinary families.
Schiff Blames Tax Code For Wealth Inequality
In a video accompanying the post, Schiff said there were certain costs associated with AI that the industry should help cover.
"There are certainly some things I think it makes sense for the AI industry to pay for," Schiff said, comparing it with the telecommunications industry’s role in the rollout of broadband.
He argued that AI-specific measures would not address the country’s underlying inequality.
"The fundamental problem is we don’t have a progressive tax code," he said.
Schiff said wealth had become heavily concentrated among a small number of families, arguing that the problem "precedes AI."
"That is because our tax system simply is broken," he said. "And we need to fix that."
He also acknowledged that it could become difficult to determine "what’s an AI company, what’s not an AI company" as AI becomes embedded across industries.
AI companies shouldn't be able to push their costs off onto everyday Americans.
And we need a truly progressive tax code that makes the economy work for ordinary families, and doesn’t result in such a staggering aggregation of wealth in the hands of a few people.
